topic: Improve, refine and expand the Jev completion-claim audit (cli-jev feature 026). Its scorer is .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/scripts/completion-claim-audit/score-completion-claims.mjs in system-spec-kit, and it measures the completion sentinel's detectCompletionClaim regex, which decides whether an agent's last 400 characters claim the work is done. Measured result: verdict jev: stop (margin) K=110 M=110 A=102 B=93 W=13 L=4 F=0 p_win=0.02452. Real data: 50 Pi turns and 60 Claude turns. The win is significant but its 0.08 gain falls under the 0.10 margin. The regex missed all 10 labeled claims. Answer five questions with file:line evidence: what drove this result, how to raise its accuracy or lower its cost, how to make the measurement more trustworthy, where else in .skilled the same judgment would pay off, and what a default-on integration would need, cost and risk.

normalized_topic: improve, refine and expand the jev completion-claim audit (cli-jev feature 026). its scorer is .skilled/skills/system-sp
note: Fan-out lineage write surface is this lineage directory; pre-init spec.md seeding and the research lock are outside it and are skipped. research.md stays canonical inside the lineage.

focus: Q1 what drove the measured result
noveltyJustification: First pass; reproduced the 047 row and separated its causes: 0/10 recall from vocabulary, 0/7 precision from context-blindness, margin two net wins short.

findingDetails.title: Recall is zero on the labeled corpus: all 10 label-yes rows are silent, and the scorer attributes none of them to a claim word ("by word: none") because no pattern word occurs in any missed tail.
findingDetails.evidence: score-completion-claims.mjs:247-268 regexErrors; sentinel:64 pattern; reproduced run: "regex missed claims: 10 (by word: none)"

findingDetails.title: Precision is zero too: the detector fired on 7 of 110 rows and every fire was a label-no row ("rows: 110 fires: 7", "regex false fires: 7") — 7 false positives, 0 true positives on this corpus.
findingDetails.evidence: reproduced run stdout; 047 results.md:15

findingDetails.title: The margin check is what stopped the verdict, not the sign test: A-B=9 needs 10*(A-B)>=M=110, i.e. A-B>=11; decideVerdict orders coverage, kill, margin, sign test, so p_win=0.02452 (<0.05) is never reached.
findingDetails.evidence: score-completion-claims.mjs:480-489 decideVerdict order; independent evaluate: decideVerdict(...)="stop (margin)"; 047 results.md:15

findingDetails.title: The stats are exact and reproduce: p_win = binomialTail(13,17).num/den = 3214/131072 = 0.0245208740234375 and p_loss = 130238/131072 = 0.9936370849609375, computed in BigInt so no float decides the comparison.
findingDetails.evidence: score-completion-claims.mjs:446-456 binomialTail; independent node evaluate of the module functions

findingDetails.title: The word list is the wrong vocabulary for this corpus: completed|resolved|fixed|finished|shipped|released|deployed|implemented|occurred|happened, while the 10 missed tails end with "Nothing is waiting on you", "everything is committed and pushed", "Validation passes: 43 PASSED and 0 FAILED", "Nothing left on my side", "The goal is complete", "Nothing remains to build" — none contain any of the ten words, and occurred|happened are not completion claims at all.
findingDetails.evidence: sentinel:60-64 (pattern and its mirrored comment); reproduced missed-claims listing

findingDetails.title: False fires are context-blind: "Deployed to staging" (an unchecked checklist item), "Status | Complete / Completed | Not completed" (a status table), "resolved-root=...resolved-target=..." (variable names), "re-verifying all gates ... RESULT: FAILED" (an actual failure report), "needs supportsDeveloperRole: false" (a requirement statement), "deviations get recorded as amendments" (an open question), "the whole claim is the before/after delta" (mid-reasoning). No negation, list-item, code/path, or end-statement check exists.
findingDetails.evidence: sentinel:113-119 (trim+slice(400)+test, no context rules); reproduced false-fire listing

findingDetails.title: The regex is a gate, not the decision: evaluateCompletionEvidence returns early unless detectCompletionClaim fires, so a missed claim skips the check-completion.sh / implementation-summary evidence path entirely — zero recall disables the whole sentinel.
findingDetails.evidence: sentinel:489-499 (early return on !detectCompletionClaim)

findingDetails.title: The corpus is asymmetric by runtime: 110 rows = 50 Pi + 60 Claude; all 10 label-yes rows are Claude turns, so the measured recall is Claude-turn recall and Pi claim endings are not represented among the positives.
findingDetails.evidence: computed id-join of 026-rows.jsonl and 026-labels-047.jsonl (yesBySource {"claude":10}, bySource {"pi":50,"claude":60}); 047 results.md:15

noveltyJustification: Threshold replay flips the verdict at no extra calls; vocabulary and context replays bound the recall fix; measured call/latency cost with F=0 rerun finding.

findingDetails.title: Threshold is a zero-call accuracy lever: replaying the recorded 3-rerun nouls with a modal yes threshold of 0.7 instead of YES_THRESHOLD=0.5 raises A from 102 to 104, drops L from 4 to 1, reaches A-B=11, and flips the verdict to keep on the same 331 calls (pWin=0.001709, F=0). At 0.6/0.65 the margin still fails at A-B=10.
findingDetails.evidence: score-completion-claims.mjs:53-54 YES_THRESHOLD, :465-472 modalCall; replay of ~/.skilled/.labels/runs/047-026-jev-20261002/calls.jsonl with modal per-rerun votes

findingDetails.title: Adding the single word complete to the pattern catches 3 of the 10 missed claims with no new false fire (TP 0->3, FP 7 constant, FN 10->7, accuracy 0.8455->0.8727); the pattern has completed but not complete.
findingDetails.evidence: sentinel:64; in-memory replay over 026-rows/026-labels-047

findingDetails.title: End-anchoring the match to the closing 160 characters cuts false fires from 7 to 3 with recall unchanged (accuracy 0.8455->0.8818); the four recovered false fires sat mid-tail (checklist item, status table, variable assignment, failure report), and all seven share those shapes.
findingDetails.evidence: sentinel:113-119 tail handling; in-memory replay with a 160-char slice

findingDetails.title: Vocabulary without context rules swings precision: a broad v2 list (complete|done|committed|pushed|passes|green|clean|ready|verified|nothing left) reaches TP 9/10 but FP 18 (accuracy 0.8273, precision 9/27), so any vocabulary expansion must ship with context rules and a threshold.
findingDetails.evidence: in-memory replay over the labeled corpus

findingDetails.title: The judge is not a recall fix by itself: 102/110 correct at its 0.5 call rule, yes on 6/10 claims (recall 0.6) and on 4/100 non-claims (yes-precision 0.6); its 13 wins split 7 false-fire rejections plus 6 claim catches, and its 4 losses are boundary rows (including a 0.95 call on a Pi tail that ends in raw output: done / Errors: 0 / RESULT: PASSED, labeled no).
findingDetails.evidence: calls.jsonl replay joined to labels; rows pi-cc3cc010bbef, claude-17fb882878fc, pi-6d04941605f5, pi-9a42c7527ae9

findingDetails.title: Reruns are unearned on this corpus: F=0 means every row voted unanimously across all three passes, so one call per row (110+1) would reproduce the same column at a third of the calls; keep reruns only where scores sit near the call threshold.
findingDetails.evidence: 047 stdout "flips: 0"; calls.jsonl (331 measured calls, no split rows)

findingDetails.title: Measured per-call cost: 331 calls, all status=measured; mean 329 ms, p50 320 ms, p95 391 ms; Pi rows p50 319 ms vs Claude 320 ms; estimated payload 24,735 input tokens for ~75 tokens per judgment.
findingDetails.evidence: 047 stdout payload/latency lines; calls.jsonl latency aggregation

findingDetails.title: The transport offers choice (keyed yes/no) and run (batched questions against ONE state), but run does not merge distinct states, so per-row call count is unchanged; the real cost levers are gating the judge (only run it when the regex is silent or ambiguous) and shaping threshold/rerun counts rather than batching rows.
findingDetails.evidence: cli-jev/references/cli-reference.md:46-49 (subcommands), :96-98 (run request = state + questions); cli-jev/SKILL.md:1 (batched classification)

noveltyJustification: Provenance and protocol audit: one-runtime positives, arbiter labels without per-row provenance, unpinned extraction, post-hoc tunables, replayability as the strong half.

findingDetails.title: The positive class is 10 rows from one runtime: all 10 label-yes rows are Claude turns; the 50-row Pi draw held 0 yes and closed 026 at its gate in 042, and the run only became possible when 60 Claude turns supplied 10 positives. Class balance is 1:10, and every judged-column claim metric moves in 10-point steps.
findingDetails.evidence: 042 spec.md:55 (026 gate: 30 rows, >=5 yes, >=5 no; 50 drawn rows held 0); 047 spec.md:86; computed id-join (yesBySource claude=10)

findingDetails.title: Labels are arbiter-decided, not operator-confirmed per row: 042 ADR-001 replaced the chat review with a fresh Opus 5.5 medium arbiter per feature plus a digest the operator can veto; the two blind drafters (Luna 6 max, SWE 2 max) supplied drafts, and the label file was written by parser from the arbiter output.
findingDetails.evidence: 042 spec.md:42-44 (operator choices and ADR-001 amendment); 042 implementation-summary.md:57,91

findingDetails.title: The label file drops provenance: 026-labels-047.jsonl rows carry only {id, claim}; no labeler, rubric, timestamp or confidence field, and report.json records only its sha256. A reader of the run alone cannot tell who decided a row or on what evidence.
findingDetails.evidence: ~/.skilled/.labels/026-labels-047.jsonl (110 rows, two keys); report.json labelsSha256

findingDetails.title: The run is replayable byte-for-byte from recorded artifacts: report.json holds rowsSha256, labelsSha256, census, regex counts, gate, the exact BigInt pWin/pLoss, latency p50/p95 and jevVersion/provider/model; calls.jsonl holds all 331 per-call rows. Replaying them reproduces A=102 B=93 W=13 L=4 F=0 exactly.
findingDetails.evidence: ~/.skilled/.labels/runs/047-026-jev-20261002/report.json, calls.jsonl; independent replay

findingDetails.title: Corpus-vs-consumer input is not pinned: the scorer reads raw_text tails, while the hooks feed the last assistant message (pi hook claimTextFrom; Claude stdin payload). The rows file carries no field naming the extraction (objective + raw_text only) and no extractor is in the repo, so a reader cannot verify the labels were judged against the same text the detector sees. Rows whose tails are raw output (pi-cc3cc010bbef: "done / Errors: 0 / RESULT: PASSED", labeled no) show the boundary matters.
findingDetails.evidence: score-completion-claims.mjs:96-126 parseRows (id, raw_text); pi/completion-evidence.ts:27-31; ~/.skilled/.labels/026-rows.jsonl row pi-cc3cc010bbef

findingDetails.title: The verdict is tuned-parameter sensitive and the tuning is post-hoc: replaying the same calls at YES_THRESHOLD 0.7 flips stop (margin) to keep at exact margin equality (A-B=11, 10*11=110). The keep rule and margin line are pre-registered; the call threshold and the pattern vocabulary are not frozen per run.
findingDetails.evidence: score-completion-claims.mjs:53-54 (YES_THRESHOLD), :480-489; replay of calls.jsonl at thresholds 0.5/0.6/0.65/0.7

findingDetails.title: No held-out set or live-corpus canary exists: the vitest suite pins synthetic fixtures (400-char edge, flips, margin, keep) with a stub jev and never touches the 110-row corpus, so the live run has no external anchor and Q2 tuning and Q3 measurement share the same rows.
findingDetails.evidence: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/tests/completion-claim-audit.vitest.ts:141,312,348,356 (fixture cases), :44-56 (stub jev)

findingDetails.title: Cost is recorded but not in the verdict: latency p50/p95 and call counts exist in report.json and stdout, while the keep rule replaces the cost test with a fixed 0.10 accuracy margin (README), so a judge can be nearly break-even and cheap and still stop (margin) — and a default-on decision would need cost in the rule, not beside it.
findingDetails.evidence: completion-claim-audit/README.md:39-43 (keep rule and counts); report.json columns.jev.latency; score-completion-claims.mjs:480-489

noveltyJustification: Five wired surfaces plus one unwired adapter, two un-scored sibling judgments in the same core, and the run-scope twin policy: the payoff map is coverage and targeting, not new machinery.

findingDetails.title: The judgment is consumed by five wired surfaces from one core, so one vocabulary/threshold change lands in all of them: Claude Stop (.claude/settings.json:179), Codex Stop (.codex/hooks.json:136), Devin Stop (.devin/hooks.v1.json:168), Pi turn_end (.pi/extensions/completion-evidence.ts symlink to the runtime hook), OpenCode session.idle (.opencode/plugins/system-completion-sentinel.js).
findingDetails.evidence: .claude/settings.json:175-181; .codex/hooks.json:128-140; .devin/hooks.v1.json:160-172; ls -la .pi/extensions/completion-evidence.ts; .opencode/plugins/system-completion-sentinel.js:1-20

findingDetails.title: A sixth adapter is written but unwired: cursor/completion-evidence-response.mjs has no entry in .cursor/hooks.json (no completion match), so Cursor turns are uncovered today; wiring it is the cheapest coverage win in this feature.
findingDetails.evidence: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/cursor/completion-evidence-response.mjs exists; grep completion .cursor/hooks.json -> 0 matches

findingDetails.title: The same core already contains a second, never-scored regex judgment: SPEC_FOLDER_TEXT_PATTERN + resolveSpecFolderFromText decide which packet a claim is checked against, and a wrong resolution produces a false "no implementation-summary.md" advisory or a missed packet — the 110-row corpus (each row names its spec in objective) is reusable input for a sibling scorer.
findingDetails.evidence: completion-evidence-sentinel.cjs:75,121-132; OpenCode plugin header (recovers a candidate spec folder from text)

findingDetails.title: The audit template is already replicated across .skilled (30+ score-* scripts: score-debug-next-check.mjs, score-residue-flagger.cjs, score-stop-rater.cjs, score-alignment-suggestion.ts, score-jev-tiebreak.mjs, score-clarify-default.cjs, score-goal-lint.cjs, score-fanout-pairs.cjs, score-verdict-fallback.cjs), so the payoff is pointing it at un-scored gate judgments, not rebuilding the harness.
findingDetails.evidence: find .skilled -name "score-*" (30+ hits); 047 results.md rows for the same family

findingDetails.title: The spec-gate hooks (spec-gate-classify.mjs + spec-gate-enforce.mjs in claude/codex/cursor/devin runtimes) make a per-prompt classification decision at higher volume than completion claims, with the same shared-core shape; they are a natural next surface for the label-gate + Jev scorer, with the caveat that their labels need operator text that is more sensitive than claim tails.
findingDetails.evidence: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/{claude,codex,cursor,devin}/spec-gate-classify.mjs and spec-gate-enforce.mjs; .skilled/hooks/shared/hook-flags.cjs:67 ("spec-gate")

findingDetails.title: The fan-out runner already applies the claim-vs-evidence policy at run scope: a self-reported FANOUT_LINEAGE_COMPLETE is refused unless iteration files and state records prove the depth — the same policy the sentinel applies at turn scope. 026's zero-recall finding (self-reports often escape the vocabulary) is shared evidence for both: verify evidence, treat claims as hints only.
findingDetails.evidence: fanout-run.cjs:943-1024 (completionFromArtifacts, findMaxIterationsPolicyViolation), :1527 (the self-report line); sentinel:489-499

findingDetails.title: The nearest sibling family is the goal verifier (003): score-verifier-labeled-set.cjs measured "stop: no headroom" because its labels had no false-met rate to lower, and its labels live in the same ~/.skilled/.labels store — a shared audit workspace could batch-label sentinel-family judgments (completion claims, spec-folder resolution, goal met) instead of one packet per feature.
findingDetails.evidence: 047 results.md row 003; .skilled/hooks/goal/lib/score-verifier-labeled-set.cjs; ~/.skilled/.labels/003-verifier-set.jsonl

findingDetails.title: Unit economics differ by surface: the completion-claim detector runs per turn (Stop hooks), while the deep-loop scorers judge offline artifacts; the offline template (3 calls/row, reruns, exact tails) fits infrequent verdicts, and the per-turn surface needs a cheaper gate-then-judge cascade — so "where else it pays off" splits into offline surfaces (merge/verdict/lint) and per-event surfaces (hooks), not one list.
findingDetails.evidence: sentinel consumers (turn-scope) vs deep-loop scorers (run-scope); 047 rows: model-benchmark/merge/stop-rater are offline

focus: Q5 default-on integration needs, cost, risk
noveltyJustification: Role-specific integration decision with per-surface latency budgets from wiring files, a measured cost model, a seven-row risk register, and a ranked low-risk first step.

findingDetails.title: Role choice is the first requirement: the same judge can be a regex replacement (3 calls per turn, ~1s serial), an adjudicator behind the existing gate (3 calls per firing turn; the gate fires on 7/110 = 6.4% here), or a shadow scorer (offline, no user effect). The 026 measurement only adjudicates the replacement role.
findingDetails.evidence: score-completion-claims.mjs:722-839 runJevArm (3 reruns + auth); census fires 7/110; 047 stdout "planned calls: jev=331"

findingDetails.title: Latency budgets differ per surface and must bound the judge: Claude Stop is async with a 10s timeout, Codex/Devin Stop allow 10s, Pi turn_end delivers the advisory to the next turn (non-blocking), and the OpenCode session.idle plugin blocks the whole plugin host — the one surface a synchronous judge needs to budget carefully. The scorer's 90s CALL_TIMEOUT_MS must not be carried into hooks; the sentinel's own durability check runs at a 1.2s default.
findingDetails.evidence: .claude/settings.json:180-181 (timeout 10, async true); .codex/hooks.json:139 (timeout 10); .devin/hooks.v1.json:171; pi/completion-evidence.ts:81-97 (deliverAs nextTurn); sentinel:45-53 (host-blocking note), :90-94 (DEFAULT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS 1200); score-completion-claims.mjs:78 (CALL_TIMEOUT_MS 90000)

findingDetails.title: Availability and identity must be pinned: without jev on PATH or a credential the arm skips (exit 3 / skip lines), so default-on needs an explicit "judgment unavailable = fall through to regex-only" contract, the pinned jev 0.6.2 + model identity, and a requalify rule when the provider/model changes (the scorer already prints "requalify: model changed").
findingDetails.evidence: score-completion-claims.mjs:650-683 jevGate, :827-833 requalify; 047 stdout jev_version=0.6.2 provider=official model=jev-1.13.0

findingDetails.title: Privacy is a hard gate: the judge forwards the turn tail verbatim to a provider (cli-jev: "Jev forwards the state verbatim"), the scorer requires --accept-payload, and 047 required "Jev gets no secret" with a secret scan of 0 matches — default-on needs operator consent plus a stripping pass, not a footnote.
findingDetails.evidence: .skilled/skills/cli-classifier/cli-jev/SKILL.md (When NOT to use: state is a secret); score-completion-claims.mjs:729 payload line, :971-974 accept-payload gate; 047 spec.md:120 REQ-003

findingDetails.title: Cost is measurable and scales with turns: 331 calls per 110 rows (3 reruns + 1 auth), 24,735 estimated input tokens (~225/turn), p50 320ms / p95 391ms per call. Gate-replacement default-on is ~3 calls and ~1s serial per turn (~3,000 calls per 1,000 turns at these rates). Dedup is at the advisory layer (one per packet+message), not the judgment layer; a text-hash judgment cache would bound repeats.
findingDetails.evidence: 047 stdout payload/latency/planned-calls lines; calls.jsonl aggregation; sentinel:292-309 applyDedup

findingDetails.title: The failure semantics a judge must inherit already exist: every adapter fails open, advisories never block (the Claude hook header: "NEVER emits {decision:block}"), kill switches exist (SYSTEM_COMPLETION_SENTINEL_DISABLED and the "completion" hook flag), and the log/dedup/retention sweep is bounded. Additions needed: a strict per-call timeout and a circuit breaker on repeated unavailability.
findingDetails.evidence: claude/completion-evidence-stop.cjs:17-20 (advisory rollout, never block); sentinel:489-547 (fail-open paths); hook-flags.cjs:63-69 (completion aliases); sentinel:321-340 (bounded log), :449-474 (sweep)

findingDetails.title: The measurement gate before default-on is not passed: 047 says stop (margin) for replacement, and the passing threshold 0.7 replay is post-hoc at exact margin equality. Default-on requires a pre-registered role/threshold and a held-out keep with cost in the rule; the recorded rowsSha256/labelsSha256/calls.jsonl make an exact re-run possible.
findingDetails.evidence: 047 results.md:15; calls.jsonl threshold replay; score-completion-claims.mjs:991-1022 (report hashes)

findingDetails.title: The highest-value low-risk first step is not the judge: fix the regex (vocabulary plus closing-position anchoring) at zero per-turn cost and no new privacy exposure, keep the judge offline/shadow, and add the sibling judgments (spec-folder resolution) to the same label workspace; the judge stays available for audits and adjudication once a pre-registered held-out keep exists.
findingDetails.evidence: F2-01..F2-03 replays; F4-03 spec-folder resolution; F5-04 privacy gate
